shortDescription: Nomura expects Lodha Developers to deliver a stronger operational performance in the second half of FY27, with pre-sales and operating cash flow expected to improve, while maintaining its 'Buy' rating and target price of Rs 1,280.Following the company's second-quarter FY27 earnings call on November…

children: Nomura expects Lodha Developers to deliver a stronger operational performance in the second half of FY27, with pre-sales and operating cash flow expected to improve, while maintaining its 'Buy' rating and target price of Rs 1,280.Following the company's second-quarter FY27 earnings call on November 2, the brokerage said management had maintained its FY27 pre-sales guidance of Rs 240 billion, which implies pre-sales of Rs 143 billion in the second half, up 25% year-on-year.Nomura said the guidance looked achievable, given the company's inventory of around Rs 410 billion and launches worth Rs 190 billion in the pipeline. Total supply for the remainder of the second half of FY27 is around Rs 600 billion.To meet its guidance, Lodha needs to achieve pre-sales of Rs 143 billion in the remaining two quarters, compared with around Rs 115 billion in the second half of FY26.Management expects pre-sales of Rs 60-70 billion in each of the third and fourth quarters of FY27, with around two-thirds coming from sustenance inventory. It also expects one data centre land transaction worth around Rs 15 billion in the fourth quarter.Lodha's second-quarter pre-sales stood at Rs 50.4 billion, up 10% year-on-year and broadly in line with Nomura's estimate of Rs 51 billion. Sales were driven largely by sustenance sales, while the company launched one project in Bengaluru during the quarter.
Operating cash flow expected to rise 29%

Lodha's total collections in the second quarter stood at Rs 34.5 billion, up 1% year-on-year. Management attributed the flat growth to a high base in the year-ago quarter due to land sales in the second quarter of FY26.Operating cash flow (OCF) in the first half of FY27 stood at around Rs 27 billion, up 15% year-on-year. Management expects full-year OCF of around Rs 85 billion, implying around Rs 58 billion in the second half, a growth of 29% year-on-year.Management reiterated that the company's development business, DevCo, is likely to become net-debt-free in two to three years.
Data centre business and NCR expansion

On the data centre business, Nomura said that of the approximately 660 acres of data centre park land, Phase I development of 3.5 GW, out of the planned 5 GW, will be undertaken on 365 acres, of which 132 acres have been sold.The sanctioned input power capacity has been raised to 5 GW from 3 GW following approvals. Lodha plans to monetise a further 143 acres at around Rs 600 million per acre, generating approximately Rs 90 billion over the next three to four years.Management expects one land parcel sale worth around Rs 15 billion in the fourth quarter of FY27 at Rs 500 million per acre, compared with Rs 420 million per acre in the previous transaction. It expects one transaction approximately every six months.The proceeds are intended to largely self-fund a 1 GW data centre PowerShell on around 90 acres, which management expects to generate more than Rs 20 billion in annual rental income.Definitive documents for the first build-to-suit (BTS) data centre are expected to be signed in FY27, with construction also starting during the year. Rentals are expected to commence in FY29.Management is targeting a 1 GW BTS sign-up by FY30 and delivery by FY32, with annual rentals of Rs 20-23 billion, which it termed conservative. The remaining approximately 300 acres will be retained for future expansion.The company has also commenced pre-sales at its first NCR project, Lodha Pantheon, an office development on Golf Course Road in Gurugram.NCR remains in the pilot phase, with two more residential projects planned before the company evaluates a larger commitment.

Management expects market momentum to continue through FY27, supported by a strong festive start to the third quarter. It does not see oversupply building up, with demand concentrated among Grade A/A+ branded developers.Year-to-date realisation growth stood at around 4% year-on-year. Management expects price growth to remain contained within 5-7% annually against cost growth of around 4%, adding 100-200 basis points to margins every year. It described this improvement as structural rather than one-off.Nomura noted that Lodha's stock was trading at a 10% discount to net asset value (NAV), compared with its target price valuation based on a 20% premium. The brokerage maintained its 'Buy' rating and target price of Rs 1,280. Lodha shares closed at Rs 1,003 on November 2, 2026.

title: Nomura sees Lodha Developers' second-half pre-sales rising 25% to Rs 143 billion, maintains 'Buy'
